answer: Divergent Response Registry: each identity must answer randomized challenge sets, and its answer vector is hashed into a shared ledger anchoring a haven of prior responses. Clones producing identical vectors collapse into one identity for quota purposes. A raven process audits a sample each epoch; matching vectors beyond tolerance void all linked identities. Because a clone cannot diverge without betraying its controller, attackers must author genuinely distinct response behavior per identity, paying full model and maintenance cost against a rising tide of cross-checks.
